title: Existence of a Gaussian matrix with independent entries
statement: Let $k \ge 1$ and $d \ge 0$ be integers. Then there is a probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mu)$ carrying a measurable map $\omega \mapsto A(\omega)$, valued in the $k \times d$ real matrices, with the following properties: each entry $A_{ij}$, for $1 \le i \le k$ and $1 \le j \le d$, has law $\mathcal{N}(0, 1/k)$ (mean zero and variance $1/k$); for each row index $i$ the family of entries $(A_{ij})_{j}$ is jointly independent; and the family of rows $\bigl((A_{ij})_{j}\bigr)_{i}$ is jointly independent.
hypotheses_covered: conclusion: exists probability space and measurable matrix-valued map
entries within each row jointly independent
replaced:
For any $k > 0$ and $d \ge 0$, there exists a probability space
$(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mu)$ carrying a measurable random matrix
$A : \Omega \to \mathrm{Matrix}(\mathrm{Fin}\,k, \mathrm{Fin}\,d, \mathbb{R})$
whose entries are i.i.d.\ $\mathcal{N}(0, 1/k)$, with rows mutually independent
and entries within each row jointly independent.
